title: Strip a 14 AWG wire from a wall box to a receptacle's strip gauge and push it into the hot-side push-in hole
instruction: Strip the black wire coming from the wall box to the receptacle's 5/8 inch (16 mm) strip gauge with the wire stripper, then pick up the receptacle, push the wire fully into a push-in hole on the brass (hot) side of its back, and let go of the wire.
context: Wiring a device at a box starts with stripping each conductor to the length its terminal calls for: in O*NET 31.0, 73% of electricians (818,700 US jobs in 2024) report connecting wires to breakers and other components daily or more. The strip must be the gauge's length, unnicked, and the hot conductor must land on the brass side.
setup: Positions (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. Wall facing the robot: 1/2 in drywall, front at x 52.0, y -30 to 10, 34 cm tall, on a 2x4 stud (y -7.15 to -3.35) and plate. Blue PVC nail-on single-gang box (Carlon B118A, 95 x 57 x 73 mm) nailed to the stud, flush, opening centred at y -10.0, 12.0 cm up. 14/2 NM-B cable down the stud into the box top; sheath ends in the box; white and bare folded in. Black conductor (14 AWG solid copper, 2.69 mm over PVC and nylon): 35.7 cm from the sheath, bent by hand in plane y -10.0 through (x, height): (56.0, 11.0) at the sheath, (51.7, 10.8) box front, (50.5, 7.5), (49.2, 4.5), (47.5, 2.2), (45.2, 1.2), (42.8, 1.4), (40.8, 3.0), (39.6, 5.5), (39.8, 8.0), (40.0, 10.0), straight up to its end at (40.0, 17.0). Wire stripper (Klein 11055 pattern): 181 mm, 154 g, holes for 10-18 AWG solid (14 AWG 26 mm from the pivot, larger nearer it), straight blue and yellow handles, spring-open. Flat, jaws open pointing +x, pivot at (30.0, -10.0), 20.0 cm up, jaws overhanging a grey steel stand: 2.4 x 3.0 cm block under the pivot (top 19.7) at (29.4, -10.0), 1.2 x 7.0 cm under the handles (top 19.25) at (23.0, -11.2). Receptacle (Leviton T5320-W pattern, 15 A duplex; body 72 x 33 x 22 mm, strap 106 x 22 mm, 45 g): loose, face up on a 12 x 8 cm plywood tray (top 6.0 up, on a 6 x 4 cm block) at (25.0, -24.0), length along x. Push-in holes 10 mm either side of centre lengthwise, 11 mm across: brass (hot) pair on -y, silver on +y. Arms in the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: In simulation, at the end of the trial: 0 if the wire is in a push-in hole on the silver (neutral) side (reversed polarity), if it was nicked (closed in a smaller hole than 14 AWG) or cut between holes. Otherwise strip credit: 0.3 if the slug is fully off and the bare length is 14 to 18 mm, 0.15 if 12 to 20 mm, else 0. Termination, only with strip credit: 0.7 if the conductor is clamped in a brass-side push-in hole at least 12 mm deep, with at most 1.5 mm of copper showing between the jacket and the receptacle's back and the jacket no more than 1.5 mm inside the hole, and no fingertip within 8 mm of the wire outside the receptacle. Where the receptacle is, and whether a hand still holds it, does not matter. Success (1.0) when both hold for 1 s. Real trial, after the robot lets go of the wire: copper showing at the back by feeler or caliper (at most 1.5 mm); side by the screw colour; holding the receptacle, a 10 N tug on the wire for 5 s must not pull it out (the clamp is engaged); then release the wire with a 1/8 in screwdriver in the hole's release slot and measure the bare length by caliper and inspect the copper under a 10x loupe: any nick, ring or scrape in the copper scores 0.
reset_notes: Each trial needs a fresh conductor end: release the wire from the receptacle with a screwdriver in its release slot, put the receptacle back face up on its tray, clear the cut slug from the stripper's jaws, pull the used cable out of the box and fit a new length of 14/2 NM-B prepared the same way (sheath ending 4 cm behind the box front, black conductor cut to 35.7 cm and bent to the listed points).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. The conductor is ten hinged links from the box, springs that yield plastically at 0.05 N m so it stays bent like solid copper, ending in a rigid 70 mm end whose last 50 mm of jacket are 2 mm rings. The cut is code: jaws shut on a hole turn off the rings at the blade; the slug comes off past 10 N. Push-in clamp: a ratchet from 12 mm deep. Simplified: boxy stripper on a stand, U-notched jaws, square holes, no gauge mark; sheath and other conductors visual.
scores: Dream-1 run (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta, 2,400 steps): 0.0, the right hand moved over the receptacle on its tray without lifting it, and the stripper and wire were not used; scripted demo: 1.0 (1,248 steps).
